name: William Roberts
role: Man convicted at Miles City of stealing Hash Knife horses
bio: William (Win) Roberts was charged with stealing six horses from the Hash Knife camp in the winter of 1884-85, arrested below Rapid City in May 1885 by a Miles City deputy marshal, and tried at Miles City, with George Fitzgerald and others from Medora subpoenaed as witnesses. In October 1885 the paper reported him found guilty and, it heard, sentenced to sixteen years; it also noted that he and Tommy Hughes had earlier served six months for smuggling in Canada. In December 1885 he was among Miles City jail prisoners who tried to escape. In March 1884 the paper had disputed a Mandan report that Win Roberts and friends made a traveling man sing at gunpoint in a bar.
